Eligible permanent full-time employees receive 20 days of annual leave for each complete leave year. Annual leave is intended for planned time away from work.

About this chapter: This policy describes annual leave, sick leave, casual leave, parental leave, public holidays, carry-over, and leave requests.
4.4 ANNUAL LEAVE CARRY-OVER
4.4.1 Standard carry-over limit
Employees may carry over up to 5 unused annual-leave days from one leave year into the next leave year.
4.4.2 Conditions
Only unused annual leave from the current leave year is eligible for standard carry-over. Sick leave and casual leave cannot be converted into annual leave and cannot be carried over under this section.
The carried-over balance must be used by 31 March of the following year. Any standard carried-over annual leave remaining after 31 March expires, unless an approved exception under Section 4.3 applies.
4.4.3 Exception: business-critical inability to take leave
If an employee could not reasonably take annual leave because a manager required the employee to support a documented business-critical delivery, the employee may request an exception. The manager must provide written justification, and People Operations must approve the exception in writing before the normal expiry date.
An exception does not automatically grant unlimited carry-over. The approval must specify the additional number of days, the revised expiry date, and the reason for the exception. Employees should retain written approval for their records.
4.4.4 No automatic cash conversion
Unused annual leave does not automatically convert to cash at year-end under this policy. Any payment on separation or other cash settlement must be reviewed under the employee's applicable agreement and local requirements by People Operations and Payroll.

results.question: Can I take 6 more annual days in December?
results.answer:
**No, not right now.** You can't add 6 more annual days in December.

- **Probation cap (Employee Handbook 3.4.4):** During probation, India-payroll employees may use up to 5 days of annual leave. The rest becomes available after confirmation.
- **Your usage:** 3 days used (LR-0150, LR-0159) plus 2 pending (LR-0189, 3–4 Dec). That's 5 of 5, so no more annual leave can be used before confirmation.
- **Your probation ends 20 January 2027**, so the remaining annual leave opens after that date.

The system shows 4 annual days "available to book now," but the 3.4.4 cap applies on top of that, so I'd treat 0 as the real figure until confirmation. If you want to check, ask People Operations.

Sick and casual leave aren't affected by this cap (3.4.4). You have 9 sick and 6 casual days available.
results.expected: No: he is on probation until 20 January 2027, and his 5 probation days are already used or requested (Employee 3.4.4); more after confirmation.

results.question: Why can't I open the client systems?
results.answer:
Most likely reason: your **Information Security training is overdue by more than 30 days**, so client system access is suspended.

- **Information Security:** due 14 Oct 2026, still open, 33 days overdue. Under L&D Handbook **2.5.3**, client system access stays suspended until it's completed.
- **Secure coding:** due 13 Nov 2026, still open, 3 days overdue. It doesn't trigger the suspension yet, but it's overdue and should be completed.

Other things to check:
- **Client project access:** I found no ServiceDesk tickets on your record. Under IT and Security Handbook **4.2.2**, client project access is requested by your manager through ServiceDesk (category ACC) once you're assigned to a project. You're on Delivery route planning (Ferrowind Outfitters, 100%, from 28 Sep 2026), so ask your manager (Daniel Brooks, AMS-1008) whether that request was raised.
- **ODC badge:** Not the cause. Your project is not an ODC (IT and Security Handbook / Administration Handbook **3.4.2** only applies to ODCs).

Complete the Information Security training in AMS Learn. Access should be restored after that, but if it isn't, contact People Operations or your manager.

Employee Handbook > Chapter 4: Employee Leave Policy (India) > 4.4 Annual Leave Carry-over
About this chapter: This policy describes annual leave, sick leave, casual leave, parental leave, public holidays, carry-over, and leave requests.
4.4 ANNUAL LEAVE CARRY-OVER
4.4.1 Standard carry-over limit
Employees may carry over up to 5 unused annual-leave days from one leave year into the next leave year.
4.4.2 Conditions
Only unused annual leave from the current leave year is eligible for standard carry-over. Sick leave and casual leave cannot be converted into annual leave and cannot be carried over under this section.
The carried-over balance must be used by 31 March of the following year. Any standard carried-over annual leave remaining after 31 March expires, unless an approved exception under Section 4.3 applies.
4.4.3 Exception: business-critical inability to take leave
If an employee could not reasonably take annual leave because a manager required the employee to support a documented business-critical delivery, the employee may request an exception. The manager must provide written justification, and People Operations must approve the exception in writing before the normal expiry date.
An exception does not automatically grant unlimited carry-over. The approval must specify the additional number of days, the revised expiry date, and the reason for the exception. Employees should retain written approval for their records.
4.4.4 No automatic cash conversion
Unused annual leave does not automatically convert to cash at year-end under this policy. Any payment on separation or other cash settlement must be reviewed under the employee's applicable agreement and local requirements by People Operations and Payroll.

Up to 50% of the unused learning budget carries forward to the next budget year. Carried-forward budget must be used by the end of that next budget year; it cannot be carried forward a second time.
8.4.4 Approval and reimbursement
Learning expenses need manager approval in AMS People before payment. Employees are reimbursed after completing the course or exam and uploading the certificate or receipt.
8.4.5 Service agreement for costly certifications
A single certification or course costing more than INR 1,00,000 or USD 2,000 needs a service agreement. If the employee resigns within 12 months of completion, they repay a prorated share of the cost.

Step 2: Request approval from your manager in AMS People before booking the exam or course.

About this chapter: Degree programmes, such as an MBA or a master's degree, are not covered by the learning budget.
4.3 WHAT IS COVERED
4.3.1 Share of fees
AMS pays 50% of the tuition fees, up to INR 5,00,000 per programme in India or USD 15,000 per programme in the United States.

Application fees, books, travel, and accommodation are not covered.

Fees are reimbursed each term after the employee uploads the fee receipt and proof of passing the previous term.
